message.content:
Here are five flower species that play especially prominent roles in pollination across South America. These plants are widely visited by a variety of pollinators—hummingbirds, bees, butterflies, bats, and even some mammals—and they help sustain local ecosystems and agricultural productivity.

| # | Flower Species | Family | Key Pollinators | Why It Matters |
|---|----------------|--------|-----------------|----------------|
| **1** | *Heliconia* spp. (e.g., *Heliconia rostrata*) | Heliconiaceae | Hummingbirds, bees | Bright, trumpet‑shaped flowers attract hummingbirds; the structure also supports bee visits. Heliconias are abundant in tropical forests and serve as major nectar sources. |
| **2** | *Passiflora* spp. (e.g., *Passiflora edulis*, *P. caerulea*) | Passifloraceae | Bees, butterflies, hummingbirds | The complex floral architecture provides rewards for a wide range of insects and birds. Many *Passiflora* species are cultivated for fruit but also support wild pollinators. |
| **3** | *Annona* spp. (e.g., *Annona muricata*, *A. cherimola*) | Annonaceae | Bats, moths, bees | These trees produce large, fragrant flowers that attract nocturnal pollinators such as bats. Their fruits are also an important food source for wildlife. |
| **4** | *Cattleya* spp. (e.g., *Cattleya labiata*) | Orchidaceae | Bees, wasps | Orchids often have highly specialized pollination mechanisms. *Cattleya* species are prized horticulturally and also provide resources for native bees. |
| **5** | *Tillandsia* spp. (e.g., *Tillandsia usneoides*) | Bromeliaceae | Bees, hummingbirds | Epiphytic bromeliads form water tanks that attract a variety of pollinators. They are widespread in cloud forests and contribute to nutrient cycling. |

> **Note:**  
> - The “top” status of these species can vary by region and ecosystem type.  
> - Some of these plants are also economically important (e.g., *Passiflora edulis* for passionfruit).  
> - Conservation of these flowering species helps maintain healthy pollinator communities and overall biodiversity.
